description: Agent tools layer: Implement 8 specialized tools that the LangGraph agent orchestrates to answer queries. Each tool is a Python function with Pydantic schema for LLM tool calling. Tools: (1) sql_query - Execute SQL queries on SQLite with safety checks, (2) vector_search - Semantic search in ChromaDB collections, (3) graph_query - Traverse NetworkX graph for relationships, (4) downtime_calc - Calculate well downtime from inspections using production rules, (5) compliance_check - Detect rule violations against SOP deadlines, (6) memory_retrieval - Fetch user/well-scoped context, (7) memory_update - Record corrections/feedback, (8) conflict_detect - Find disagreements between data sources. This feature depends on FEAT-001 (SQLite data) and FEAT-002 (ChromaDB + graph).
steps: Create backend/tools/sql_query.py: Implement SQLQueryTool class with execute(query: str, params: dict) → dict. Use sqlite3 with parameterized queries (never string interpolation). Whitelist allowed SQL keywords (SELECT, WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT) and block DML (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP). Return {columns, rows, row_count} with error handling for malformed queries. Add query rewriting helper to convert natural language hints (e.g., 'last 30 days') to SQL date filters. Load well_types and rules from SQLite to apply production threshold calculation in queries.

Create backend/tools/vector_search.py: Implement VectorSearchTool class with search(query_text: str, collection_name: str, filter_metadata: dict, n_results: int) → list[dict]. Initialize ChromaDB client pointing to data/chroma/. Support collection_name in ['manuals', 'sops', 'reports', 'context']. Apply metadata filters (e.g., {asset_id: 'WELL-0001'} to search only that well's reports). Return [{document, metadata, distance}]. Include citation generation: extract source_file, asset_id, section_name from metadata to create citation string like 'T200 Manual §9.3' or 'MNT-0001-002 Report'.

Create backend/tools/graph_query.py: Implement GraphQueryTool class with traverse(start_node: str, relation: str, depth: int) → dict, get_neighbors(node_id: str, node_type: str) → list[dict], shortest_path(from_node: str, to_node: str) → list[str]. Load NetworkX graph from data/graph/knowledge_graph.json at initialization. Use precomputed indexes for common patterns (e.g., get_well_hierarchy, get_area_wells). Support queries like 'get all wells in area SW-23', 'get equipment for WELL-0001', 'get team lead for area NE-07'.

Create backend/tools/downtime_calc.py: Implement DowntimeCalculatorTool class with calculate_downtime(asset_id: str, start_date: str, end_date: str) → dict. Query inspections table for asset_id in date range. For each inspection, compute is_producing = (wellhead_temp_c - ambient_temp_c) >= threshold where threshold from well_types table. If not producing, add 7 days downtime (weekly inspection cadence). If missed inspection (gap >14 days), count 0 downtime for missing weeks per instructions. Return {total_downtime_days, producing_weeks, non_producing_weeks, missed_weeks, details: [{inspection_id, date, is_producing, temp_diff, reason}]}. Check context_notes for planned shutdowns to annotate reasons.

Create backend/tools/compliance_check.py: Implement ComplianceCheckTool class with check_violations(asset_id: str, start_date: str, end_date: str) → list[dict]. Load rules from data/rules/rules.json. For each rule, query relevant data: RC-01 (check inspection frequency: any gap >14 days), RC-02 (check maintenance for 'Annual flowline integrity test' once per year), SR-01 (check spill reports: spill ≥5 bbl must have report within 24h of discovery), SR-02 (check spill containment: any spill contained >4h after discovery). Return [{rule_id, violated, details, deadline_missed_by_hours}]. Use maintenance table report_file field to verify if report exists.

Create backend/tools/memory_retrieval.py: Implement MemoryRetrievalTool class with get_context(user_id: str, asset_id: str, scope: str) → dict. Read from data/memory/ JSON files: user_{user_id}.json (user-scoped corrections), well_{asset_id}.json (well-scoped corrections), global_rules.json (team-wide overrides). Each correction has {correction_id, created_at, author_user_id, scope, entity_id, field, old_value, new_value, reason, valid_from, valid_to}. Return corrections applicable to current query context. Also return conversation history for user_id from user_{user_id}_history.jsonl (last 10 messages).

Create backend/tools/memory_update.py: Implement MemoryUpdateTool class with record_correction(user_id: str, asset_id: str, field: str, old_value: any, new_value: any, reason: str, scope: str) → dict. Append to appropriate JSON file in data/memory/ based on scope (user, well, global). Generate unique correction_id = f'COR-{timestamp}-{random_suffix}'. Set valid_from = now, valid_to = null. Track provenance: who (user_id), when (created_at), why (reason), what (field, old→new). Return {correction_id, status: 'recorded'}. Trigger conflict_detect tool internally to check for disagreements.

Create backend/tools/conflict_detect.py: Implement ConflictDetectTool class with detect_conflicts(asset_id: str, field: str, new_value: any) → list[dict]. Compare new_value against: (1) latest inspection/maintenance data in SQLite, (2) existing corrections in memory JSON files, (3) context_notes with conflicting info. Return [{conflict_type, source, existing_value, new_value, severity}]. Severity = 'high' if contradicts inspector observation, 'medium' if contradicts operator note, 'low' if just different correction by another user.
acceptance_criteria: 8 tool files created in backend/tools/: sql_query.py, vector_search.py, graph_query.py, downtime_calc.py, compliance_check.py, memory_retrieval.py, memory_update.py, conflict_detect.py
Each tool has Pydantic schema for LLM function calling with input parameters and return type
SQLQueryTool blocks unsafe SQL (no DELETE, DROP, UPDATE allowed), uses parameterized queries
VectorSearchTool returns citations in format 'T200 Manual §9.3' or 'MNT-0001-002 Report' extracted from metadata
DowntimeCalculatorTool correctly applies production threshold: T200 requires 15°C diff, T350 requires 20°C diff (from well_types table)
ComplianceCheckTool detects violations for all 9 rules (SR-01 to SR-04, RC-01 to RC-05) with accurate deadline calculations
MemoryRetrievalTool reads from user_{user_id}.json, well_{asset_id}.json, global_rules.json in data/memory/
MemoryUpdateTool appends corrections with full provenance (who, when, why, scope) and triggers conflict detection
ConflictDetectTool assigns severity (high/medium/low) based on conflict source (inspector vs operator vs another user)
verification: Test sql_query: python -c "from tools.sql_query import SQLQueryTool; tool = SQLQueryTool(); result = tool.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) as cnt FROM wells', {}); print(result)" — expect {columns: ['cnt'], rows: [[200]], row_count: 1}

Test vector_search: python -c "from tools.vector_search import VectorSearchTool; tool = VectorSearchTool(); result = tool.search('production temperature rule', 'manuals', {}, 1); print(result[0]['metadata'])" — expect metadata with well_type_code and section_name

Test graph_query: python -c "from tools.graph_query import GraphQueryTool; tool = GraphQueryTool(); result = tool.get_neighbors('WELL-0001', 'Equipment'); print(len(result))" — expect 5 equipment nodes

Test downtime_calc for WELL-0001 Oct 2026: python -c "from tools.downtime_calc import DowntimeCalculatorTool; tool = DowntimeCalculatorTool(); result = tool.calculate_downtime('WELL-0001', '2026-10-01', '2026-10-16'); print(f'{result[\"non_producing_weeks\"]} weeks')" — expect 2 weeks (Oct 8 and Oct 15 inspections show not producing)

Test compliance_check for RC-01: python -c "from tools.compliance_check import ComplianceCheckTool; tool = ComplianceCheckTool(); result = tool.check_violations('WELL-0001', '2024-01-01', '2024-01-31'); print([v for v in result if v['rule_id']=='RC-01'])" — expect violation if any gap >14 days between inspections

Test memory operations: Create test correction with python -c "from tools.memory_update import MemoryUpdateTool; tool = MemoryUpdateTool(); cid = tool.record_correction('U-101', 'WELL-0001', 'wellhead_temp_c', 24.0, 41.0, 'Faulty thermal gun', 'well'); print(cid)" then retrieve with python -c "from tools.memory_retrieval import MemoryRetrievalTool; tool = MemoryRetrievalTool(); ctx = tool.get_context('U-101', 'WELL-0001', 'well'); print(len(ctx['corrections']))" — expect 1 correction returned
